structured.school_or_org: Youth for Energy Southeast Asia (Y4E-SEA); De La Salle-College of Saint Benilde (School of Diplomacy and Governance host); Green Economy Ready; Embassy of Italy in Manila; global leads IRENA and Italian MFA (with SDG7 Youth Constituency and UNICEF)
structured.year_or_edition: 2025 peer educators selected by IRENA; inaugural Philippines workshop 23 May 2026
structured.program_event: Italy-IRENA Action for Climate Toolkit (I ACT) — Philippines first rollout (Y4E-SEA’s fourth Southeast Asian rollout after Indonesia, Vietnam, Singapore)
structured.theme_or_track: Youth climate literacy, renewable energy transition, peer-to-peer education; six modules: dispelling myths; climate and renewable energy intro; renewable energy for climate action; energy for development; just and inclusive transitions; youth engagement
structured.what_it_does: I ACT is a global train-the-trainers program: IRENA and Italy equip selected youth peer educators with a six-module toolkit so they can run peer-led, non-formal workshops on climate action, energy transition, and the SDGs. The May 2026 Manila workshop trained 80+ Filipino youth leaders, with government speakers (DOE, ERC, DENR) contextualizing the Philippine energy landscape, and encouraged delegates to form a local I ACT Peer Educator Network to cascade further trainings and climate–energy projects.
structured.place: Manila, Philippines (Ideation Hall, Atrium Campus, De La Salle-College of Saint Benilde)
structured.outcome_or_award: Philippines’ first I ACT training program; over 82 young climate leaders trained; closing pledges to become peer educators/changemakers; informal awards and partner certificates of appreciation reported; path toward a Philippine I ACT Peer Educator Network (not a ranked competition prize)
structured.gap: No public roster of all ~82–80+ workshop participants or named follow-on student projects launched after May 2026. Full IRENA article body not fully retrievable (403 on direct fetch; only search snippets). Exact 2025 Peer Educator selection dates/criteria for the three Filipino educators not detailed beyond “selected by IRENA.” No verified link to Climate Change Commission Youth CLAP, competitive placement, or multi-year PH edition before 2026. Participant projects (beyond the workshop itself) are not published as separate named initiatives.
structured.note: Useful for Youth CLAP student teams: this is capacity-building / train-the-trainer, not a pitch competition. Entry points include future IRENA I ACT Peer Educator calls, Y4E-SEA Philippines workshops, and campus peer-education groups using the six modules. Named PH facilitators (Buensuceso, Salaysay, Tupas) and partners (Benilde SDG, Green Economy Ready, Italian Embassy) are the practical contacts surface. Spotlight speakers at the launch included DOE’s Liza V. Pangilinan, ERC’s Sharon Ocampo-Montañer, DENR’s Noralene Uy and Ann Hazel D. Javier, and WeGeneration’s Christianne Santos (solar case study). One quoted participant: Stephen Godfrey Oafallas (food security / undergraduate). Benilde student participants interviewed: Andre Martinez and Eurice Coyoca (AB-DIA).
